summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest tightness, bilateral leg edema, and a 10-pound weight gain over one week, initially raising concern for cardiac ischemia. Evaluation revealed normal cardiac enzymes and EKG, with symptoms attributed to anxiety and depression. She was found to have a UTI caused by ESBL-producing E. coli, prompting IV meropenem therapy. Due to her history of ESBL-related sepsis, a 10-day antibiotic course was planned, requiring a PICC line for outpatient ertapenem. The PICC was placed on the morning of discharge after a delay. Her edema, likely exacerbated by high salt intake and obstructive sleep apnea, improved significantly with IV and oral furosemide, resulting in a 25-pound weight loss. A DVT was ruled out, and her subtherapeutic INR at discharge was attributed to antibiotic-warfarin interaction. Chronic conditions including HIV, hepatitis C, and cirrhosis were stable. Follow-up was arranged for pulmonary (CPAP adjustment), orthopedics (shoulder pain), psychiatry, and a CT chest for a persistent RUL opacity.
